textbookText: Beneficial 1. Earthworms are food for many animals like birds, lizards frogs snakes and aquarium fishes. Similarly, they are used as fishing baits by fisherman or anglers. 2. Earthworms make soil porous, loose and fertile by their continuous movement and castings or excreta in soil. So physical and chemical characteristics of soil is improved which is beneficial for farmers. 3. Nowadays, earthworms are widely used in vermi-composting i.e. used to prepare compost manure from organic residues. 4. In the ancient times, they were used to prepare medicines of piles, jaundice, rheumatic fever, gallstone, infertility etc. 5. Earthworms can be considered as representative invertebrate specimen and dissected in the biology laboratory to study their anatomy and physiology.

Harmful 1. Many burrows formed by earthworm causes seepage and loss of water from irrigated land resulting reduced crop yield. 2. Loose soil formed by earthworm is easily eroded by water from sloping land. 3. Earthworm come out from the burrow on the earth surface with several parasites like Amoebotania, gapeworm, nematodes etc. and germs like bacteria viruses in their body which may infect other animals. 4. Some species of earthworm damage the roots of cultivated plants such as paddy, betelvine etc.
